clue.text: 'Mad Proposal' that might have been Spinning Around by Kylie

definitions.note: the definition points to another Kylie Minogue hit; 'might have been' admits the answer is a different song of hers

parts.note: loco is Spanish-derived slang for crazy
a motion is a proposal put to a meeting

explanation.surface: A tongue-in-cheek suggestion that a crazy proposal could have been Kylie Minogue's song Spinning Around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinning Around' is a real Kylie Minogue single, so the answer is another of her hits, The Loco-Motion; 'might have been' says the definition is a stand-in by example, and both songs involve moving round.
explanation.definitionFit: Kylie Minogue had a hit with The Loco-Motion, so it is a song of hers alongside Spinning Around.

clue.text: Between parties one gets the urge

indicators.note: between says the next piece sits in the middle of the two party words

parts.note: Lib is short for Liberal, a political party
a do is a party or celebration
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone gets a sudden urge in the gap between two parties.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'parties' does double duty, standing for a political party and for a social gathering, with the numeral for one placed between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual desire, a strong instinctive drive or craving.

clue.text: Small group with unfinished purpose infiltrated by copper

indicators.note: infiltrated by means the next piece gets inside the shortened word
unfinished means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a cause is an aim or purpose
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A small group with a half-formed aim finds a policeman has got in among them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer; here it is the metal, symbol CU. 'Unfinished' trims CAUSE to CAUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A caucus is a small group of party members meeting to decide policy.

clue.text: Inn MP suggests?

parts.note: the letters MP are the middle two of the word temple, so the phrase middle of temple describes them

explanation.surface: A question about what a Member of Parliament might suggest regarding an inn.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: MP are the central letters of TEMPLE, so they 'suggest' the middle of temple. Middle Temple is one of London's four Inns of Court, the societies to which barristers belong.
explanation.definitionFit: Middle Temple is one of the four Inns of Court, the London professional societies for barristers.

clue.text: Caustic hypocrite. Not half

indicators.note: not half means only the first half of the name is used

parts.note: Tartuffe is Moliere's religious hypocrite, whose name means a hypocrite

explanation.surface: A cutting remark about a hypocrite, ending with the British exclamation 'Not half!'
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is British slang for 'very much'; here it means keep only half of TARTUFFE, the title hypocrite of Moliere's play.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart remark is sharp and biting, the same as a caustic one.

clue.text: Fraction following 30/11, it may seem

parts.note: the day after 30 November is 1 December, written 1/12, which looks like a fraction

explanation.surface: A puzzle about which fraction comes after thirty elevenths.
explanation.walkthrough: 30/11 reads as a fraction but is a date in British order, 30 November; the next day, 1 December, is written 1/12.
explanation.definitionFit: The date written 1/12 looks like the fraction one over twelve, a single part out of twelve.

clue.text: Powder mixed in 11

indicators.note: mixed says the letters found are rearranged
in says only a run of letters lying within the answer to 11 is used, the rest set aside

parts.note: the answer to 11 down, the Essex seaside town

explanation.surface: Powder blended into some other item numbered eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters LACT sit inside CLACTON-ON-SEA (the answer to 11 down, an Essex seaside resort); 'mixed' rearranges them.
explanation.definitionFit: Talc is the soft mineral ground into talcum powder for the skin.

clue.text: It was formerly in the fleet, a Ka rebuilt with lorry parts

definitions.text: It was formerly in the fleet

indicators.note: rebuilt says the parts are put together again in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the Ford Ka car

explanation.surface: A small Ford Ka reconstructed from bits of a lorry, once part of a fleet of vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'fleet' looks like a company's vehicles; it is the Royal Navy. 'Rebuilt' rearranges A, KA and LORRY.
explanation.definitionFit: Ark Royal is the name of several Royal Navy aircraft carriers, the last one retired in 2011.

clue.text: Containers not on order for another

indicators.note: with not, order says the letters of containers lose those of on and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some containers are not on order, so another must be found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not on order' means CONTAINERS without O and N, then rearranged. The definition 'another' leans on 'Containers': the answer is another kind of container.
explanation.definitionFit: A canister is a type of storage vessel, so it is another of the containers just named.

clue.text: Marches, tied to sign

parts.note: bound means tied up
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Protest marches tied to a placard or sign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marches' looks like a verb or protests; it is the noun for border regions, as in the Welsh Marches.
explanation.definitionFit: Marches are border territories, the frontier lands between two countries.

clue.text: Corresponding with dark Finns on a regular basis

indicators.note: on a regular basis means take every other letter of the words

explanation.surface: Writing letters regularly to some dark-haired Finns.
explanation.definitionFit: Akin to means similar to, matching or of the same kind as something.

clue.text: Unexpectedly cool at Cannes or here?

indicators.note: unexpectedly says the letters fall in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: Wondering whether it is surprisingly chilly on the Riviera or in some other resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Clacton-on-Sea is an Essex seaside resort, a homely British contrast to glamorous Cannes; 'here' points at the place the shuffled letters make.
explanation.definitionFit: The word here stands for a place, and the answer is a seaside town in Essex.

clue.text: Ringer cutting garment

indicators.note: cutting means the last letter is cut away

parts.note: a doublet is a close-fitting jacket once worn by men

explanation.surface: A bell-ringer slicing through a piece of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ringer' suggests a bell-ringer; it is a 'dead ringer', a lookalike.
explanation.definitionFit: A ringer is someone who looks exactly like another person, a lookalike.

clue.text: Birds roll about on board

indicators.note: on board says the piece goes inside the letters of a ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship, the ship one is on board
to wallow is to roll about, as in mud

explanation.surface: Birds rolling around on the deck of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Swallows are small fork-tailed migratory songbirds.

clue.text: Tea guzzling bishop with surplice, reddish-brown

indicators.note: guzzling says the first word swallows the next piece

parts.note: RR stands for Right Reverend, the title of a bishop
a cotta is a short surplice worn by clergy

explanation.surface: A bishop in his surplice gulping tea until he turns reddish-brown.
explanation.walkthrough: A cotta is a short white surplice; RR, Right Reverend, is the style of a bishop.
explanation.definitionFit: Terracotta is the brownish-orange colour of unglazed fired clay.

clue.text: Race headlong to quirky Chelsea …

parts.note: steep means sharply sloping, plunging headlong

indicators.note: quirky says the letters of the place appear in an odd order

explanation.surface: Someone racing headlong to a quirky part of London, the thought carried on in the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: Chelsea is a district of London. The ellipsis leads into 18 across, which is another race.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeplechase is a horse race over fences, or a running race over hurdles and water jumps.

clue.text: Granular leather that's shabby, cut in two, and unseasoned

indicators.note: cut in two means the word is halved and its second half dropped

parts.note: shaggy means rough and unkempt, much like shabby
green wood is unseasoned, not yet dried

explanation.surface: Describing a worn leather that is shabby, split, and not properly cured.
explanation.definitionFit: Shagreen is untanned leather with a rough, grainy surface, or sharkskin used the same way.

clue.text: Headless bird is left on earth up at castle

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the pieces are read from bottom to top
headless means the first letter goes

parts.note: a heron is a long-legged wading bird
E is the abbreviation for earth, as in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: A beheaded bird and a dying figure left on the ground near a castle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' turns the whole string ERON + IS + L + E, as the answer is entered downwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Elsinore is the Danish castle where Shakespeare sets Hamlet.

clue.text: … semi with bar

definitions.note: the dots carry on from 15 across, where the word race supplies this definition

parts.note: semi is a prefix meaning half
Marathon was the old British name of the Snickers chocolate bar

explanation.surface: Continuing 15: a race headlong to Chelsea, and a semi-detached house with a pub bar.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'Race', borrowed from 15 across across the dots. Marathon was the British name of the Snickers chocolate bar until 1990.
explanation.definitionFit: A half-marathon is a running race of about thirteen miles, half the full distance.

clue.text: Beauty treatment for calf with A1 make-up

indicators.note: make-up hints at a new making of the letters, as well as cosmetics

parts.note: A plus I, the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A beauty treatment for the lower leg, with top-class cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' looks like cosmetics, which suits the beauty scene, but it says to rearrange CALF and A1 (A and I).
explanation.definitionFit: A facial is a cosmetic treatment cleansing and massaging the face.

clue.text: Old womaniser — topless sportsman

indicators.note: topless in a down clue means the top letter is removed

parts.note: a dangler is an old word for a man who hangs about after women

explanation.surface: An elderly philanderer turns up as a topless athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler fishes with rod and line, and fishing counts as a sport.

clue.text: No movement when solving's impeded?

parts.note: a traffic jam with nothing moving, and, read as two words, a crossword grid that the solver is stuck on

explanation.surface: A solver stuck on a crossword, making no progress.
explanation.definitionFit: Total traffic jam is the usual sense, while a grid that is locked describes the stuck solver.

clue.text: Lands to commit matricide

indicators.note: to commit says the act is carried out, with mother placed inside the killing phrase

parts.note: to do in is slang for to kill
ma is a familiar word for mother, the victim in matricide

explanation.surface: A grim instruction to kill one's mother for the lands she owns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do in' is slang for kill and 'ma' for mother, so murdering one's mother is to do ma in.
explanation.definitionFit: A domain is a territory under one ruler or owner, so it means lands.

clue.text: Duty yielded by dividend not introduced

indicators.note: not introduced means the opening letter is missing

parts.note: a bonus is an extra dividend paid to shareholders or policyholders

explanation.surface: A tax duty generated from a dividend that was never brought in.
explanation.definitionFit: An onus is a burden or responsibility, a duty one must bear.

clue.text: Tender rejected for London landmark

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the word is turned round

parts.note: tender means sore to the touch

explanation.surface: A bid or tender for a London landmark is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender' looks like an offer; it means painful. The statue in Piccadilly Circus is popularly called Eros.
explanation.definitionFit: The winged statue in Piccadilly Circus, London, is known as Eros.

clue.text: No movement for partnerships by pay-desk

parts.note: in cricket a stand is a partnership between two batsmen
a till is the cash register at a shop counter

explanation.surface: Partnerships are stuck at a standstill near the shop checkout.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a stand is a run-scoring partnership between two batsmen at the crease.
explanation.definitionFit: A standstill is a halt where all motion stops completely.

clue.text: Cry out for the French to leave stacks

indicators.note: to leave says those letters depart from the word

parts.note: needles are tall pointed rock stacks, like the Needles off the Isle of Wight
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: Asking for a French person to clear off from the haystacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stacks' suggests haystacks; it means sea stacks, like the Needles off the Isle of Wight, an island on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: To cry out for something is to require it badly, to be in want of it.

clue.text: Jazz musician composed Waterfalls

indicators.note: composed means put together, so the letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A jazz musician wrote a piece called Waterfalls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' looks like what a musician does; here it rearranges the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas 'Fats' Waller was an American jazz pianist and composer of the 1920s and 1930s.
